note.backdrop: Before Monday's open the S&P 500 fund is down 0.7%, the Nasdaq 100 fund 1.3% and small caps 0.5%; S&P futures are down 0.6% and the VIX is up 6.9%. No market-wide move and no fear flag. The fall is narrow: AI hardware (the median of 59 chip stocks -4.0%, printed circuit boards -3.8%) and crypto-linked stocks (the median of 34 'Finance Services' stocks -5.5%). Rates are not what is moving this morning: the 10-year yield is flat, the dollar +0.1%, gold -0.3%. Oil is -0.9%; a report says it fell after the president signalled the US would not start an attack on Iran (Stocktwits). Bitcoin is the driver that moved: -5.8% on the check's line, and on the 15-minute chart $68,526 at Friday's 4pm close against about $64,300 now, -6.2%, with most of the fall on Saturday. This time the check's bitcoin line is measured from Friday's close, unlike the last check. The week's known events are Nvidia's results on Tuesday Nov 17 after the close, Anthropic's public offering, and the Fed's October minutes (Stocktwits). Of the two stocks outside their 9-in-10 range, one is a real move (CG Oncology) and one is a distribution leaving the price (Icahn Enterprises).

read.says: AMD and Broadcom fell before the open in a wider chip sell-off; Commerzbank Research called the fallout from the leadership turmoil at Nvidia the dominant driver of risk sentiment, with investors moving into rival chip makers and then unwinding those positions too; reports that the former chief may return have not lifted Nvidia; AMD and Broadcom were still about 13% higher over five sessions and the Philadelphia chip index about 7%.

AI-linked stocks extended losses before the open on concern about the sector's growth and financing risks: Nvidia -1.8% ahead of Tuesday's results, AMD -4%, Micron -5%, Sandisk -5.3%, Western Digital -4.4%, CoreWeave -4.7% with peers IREN and Nebius; Capital.com called Nvidia the biggest immediate source of uncertainty.

Futures edged lower on Sunday night ahead of Nvidia's results on Nov 17 under its interim chief, Anthropic's public offering at a valuation of about $1.4 trillion, and the Fed's October minutes; oil fell after the president signalled the US would not start an attack on Iran; the three indexes ended last week more than 2% higher.

Crypto stocks fell before the open as bitcoin traded near $64,600, close to a three-month low, on expectations of a Fed rate rise in December (some traders pricing a half-point move) and uncertainty over crypto rules; Strategy fell more than 7%, Circle 7.6%, Coinbase 6.4%.

MSCI will delete Strategy from its equity indexes at month-end under new rules for companies that mostly hold financial assets; JPMorgan estimates up to $8.8 billion of outflows if other index providers follow, against Strategy's earlier estimate of about $2.8 billion; Strategy's $5.07 billion of dollar assets cover 3.4 years of dividends and interest.

In the week of Nov 9-15 Strategy sold 2,087,040 common shares for $244.7 million net: $206.3 million went to buying back its STRC preferred stock, $33.4 million to 485 bitcoin at $68,887 each and $5.0 million to cash; it holds 850,849 bitcoin at an average cost of $75,452.

The FDA's complete response letter says ivonescimab's application cannot be approved in its present form: effectiveness is not established without a statistically significant improvement in overall survival; the HARMONi trial met its progression-free survival goal and showed a survival trend short of significance (hazard ratio 0.76 in a later analysis).

CG Oncology's Phase 3 trial PIVOT-006 met its main goal: cretostimogene cut the risk of recurrence by 68% (hazard ratio 0.32, 95% interval 0.23-0.45, p<0.0001) in intermediate-risk and high-grade Ta bladder cancer with no grade 3 or higher treatment-related side effects; about 50,000 patients have no approved treatment of this kind; a second FDA application is planned for the second quarter of 2027.

UroGen's Zusduri made $68.0 million in the third quarter, up 35% on the quarter; its next formulation UGN-103 is under FDA review for low-grade intermediate-risk bladder cancer (goal date June 14, 2027), and it plans a 2027 trial of UGN-103 as adjuvant therapy in newly diagnosed intermediate-risk disease.

Icahn Enterprises declared a quarterly distribution of $0.50 per depositary unit, payable about Dec 23, 2026 to holders of record at the close of Nov 16, 2026, in cash or units at the holder's choice; its third-quarter net loss was $225 million.
Genco declared a record dividend of $1.05 per share for the third quarter, payable about Nov 23, 2026 to holders of record on Nov 16, 2026.

Aramark's outlook for fiscal 2027: organic revenue growth of 9% to 10%, adjusted operating income growth of 15% to 19% and adjusted earnings per share growth of 20% to 25%; a new $1 billion buyback and a 17% higher dividend; incentive pay tied to outperformance took $0.07 off fourth-quarter earnings per share.

Chaince Digital's quarterly report: about $34 million of cash and $14 million of short-term investments at Sept 30, a net loss of about $2.2 million over nine months, and conditions that at first raised substantial doubt about continuing as a going concern, which management says its plans and cash alleviate.
Bitcoin on the 15-minute chart: $68,526 at Friday's 4pm New York close, a low of $62,040 on Saturday evening New York time, $64,297 at 8:45am on Monday.
Chaince Digital on Friday's 5-minute chart: $5.26 at the open, a low of $3.69 at 2:00pm New York time, $4.27 near the close; no trade before Monday's open.

singles.beneath: The stock had already fallen about 21% over the three sessions before the letter (-9.1%, -8.6%, -5.4%); I have not found why. A headline says it was down 20% in Sunday-night trading, so part of that has come back. It was worth about $11.3 billion at Friday's close, with $150.8 million of cash at Sept 30 (investments not counted) against losses of $832.7 million over four quarters. The company says its wider program continues and cites five positive Phase 3 studies between it and Akeso.
singles.cause: Summit fell 13.1% before the open. On Sunday Nov 15 it said the FDA had issued a complete response letter for ivonescimab with chemotherapy in a form of lung cancer: the application cannot be approved in its present form because, in the FDA's view, effectiveness is not established without a statistically significant improvement in overall survival. The trial (HARMONi) met its other main goal, slowing the disease, and showed a survival trend that did not reach significance.

singles.beneath: With one-day settlement a buyer today no longer receives the distribution, so the price steps down by about that amount; that step is my inference, since the release gives only the record date. The scan's ranges are built on prices adjusted for distributions, but the check compares the latest trade with Friday's close without taking a distribution off. So this flag is the check's artifact, not a move. The yield is the thing to know: $2.00 a year on a $4.74 unit is 42%, from a company that lost $1.0 billion over four quarters; holders may take units instead of cash.
singles.cause: Icahn Enterprises is flagged at -11.8%, outside its 9-in-10 range, with no news. It is the distribution leaving the price: $0.50 per unit goes to holders of record at the close of Monday Nov 16 (its Nov 3 release), and $0.50 is 10.5% of Friday's $4.74 close. Net of it the units are down about 1%.

singles.beneath: The same artifact as Icahn Enterprises: a dividend leaving the price, read by the check as a move.
singles.cause: Genco is flagged at -4.4% with no news. Its record $1.05 dividend goes to holders of record on Nov 16 (its Nov 4 release); $1.05 is 4.0% of Friday's $26.14 close. Net of the dividend it is about flat.

singles.beneath: No page I read says why a beat was sold. The stock had risen 46% this year (AP), and the release says incentive pay tied to the outperformance took $0.07 off earnings per share. The direction is not explained; the move rests on seven pre-market prints.
singles.cause: Aramark fell 5.5% before the open after reporting its fiscal fourth quarter. The results beat analysts' estimates (AP and Zacks: adjusted earnings of 78 cents against 75 expected, revenue of $5.29 billion against $5.27 billion). Its outlook for fiscal 2027 is organic revenue growth of 9% to 10%, adjusted operating income growth of 15% to 19% and adjusted earnings per share growth of 20% to 25%, with a new $1 billion buyback and a 17% higher dividend.

singles.beneath: Naming a candidate is an early step, before trials in people. The move rests on three pre-market prints, the last at 7:00am New York time, and Ideaya is one of CG Oncology's partners (they moved together over the past year) on a morning when CG Oncology jumped. Which of these carried it I cannot tell.
singles.cause: Ideaya rose 6.6% before the open. On Sunday it named a new development candidate, IDE101, aimed at tumors that have lost the CDKN2A gene, which it puts at about 10% to 15% of solid tumors.

themes.beneath: Three known events sit just ahead (Stocktwits): Nvidia's results on Tuesday Nov 17 after the close, its first under an interim chief; Anthropic's public offering this week at a reported valuation of about $1.4 trillion; and the Fed's October minutes. In proportion, AMD and Broadcom were still about 13% higher over the last five sessions and the chip index about 7% (Invezz), so this morning takes back part of last week's rise. No page I read reports a new fact about demand, so I read the selling as caution ahead of the report; that reading is my inference.
themes.cause: Before the open the whole AI hardware group is lower: CoreWeave -6.9%, Sandisk -6.6%, Micron -6.4%, Marvell -6.2%, Super Micro -5.5%, Western Digital -5.5%, Seagate -5.5%, Intel -5.4%, AMD -5.2%, Dell -4.6%, Nvidia -3.8%, Broadcom -3.3%; the median of 59 chip stocks is -4.0%. Commerzbank Research, quoted by Invezz, calls the fallout from the leadership turmoil at Nvidia the dominant driver: investors first moved from Nvidia into its rivals, then sold those too. Reports that the former chief may return have not lifted Nvidia (Invezz). A second report cites concern about the sector's growth and how it is financed (Rallies).
themes.mechanism: Last note's question is answered: AMD and Broadcom are falling with Nvidia, and AMD by more, so this is one group being marked down, not money moving between rivals. The largest falls are not Nvidia's. They are in memory and storage (Sandisk, Micron, Western Digital, Seagate) and in CoreWeave, which the report groups with other sellers of AI computing capacity. The buyers of the hardware barely move: Microsoft +0.1%, Apple +0.3%, Alphabet, Meta and Amazon -0.6% each. My inference: the worry has shifted from who runs Nvidia to how much hardware gets bought, which reaches the suppliers and not their customers.
themes.name: AI hardware marked down again before Nvidia reports
themes.watch: Nvidia's numbers and outlook on Tuesday evening. Whether the fall spreads to the buyers (Microsoft, Alphabet, Amazon, Meta). Whether memory and storage keep falling more than Nvidia. Any statement from Nvidia's board about the chief's post.

themes.beneath: Strategy has two things of its own under the bitcoin move. MSCI will delete it from its equity indexes at month-end under new rules for companies that mostly hold financial assets; JPMorgan estimates up to $8.8 billion of selling if other index providers follow, against Strategy's own earlier estimate of $2.8 billion (24/7 Wall St). And its weekly filing shows what its share sales now pay for: of $244.7 million raised from 2,087,040 new shares in the week of Nov 9-15, $206.3 million (84%) went to buying back its own STRC preferred stock and $33.4 million to 485 bitcoin. It holds 850,849 bitcoin at an average cost of $75,452; at about $64,300 bitcoin is 15% below that. themes.beneath: In proportion: CG Oncology was worth about $6.6 billion at Friday's close, so the rise adds about $1.9 billion. UroGen was worth about $1.3 billion, so its fall takes off about $0.13 billion. CG Oncology had $28.2 million of cash at Sept 30 with investments not counted, and has sold new shares four times in three years; the mosaic put its chance of a share-sale filing in the next 20 sessions at 8.6% before this move, against 0.9% for the usual stock. That is a chance that a filing comes, measured before the result, and not a direction.
themes.cause: CG Oncology rose 29.0% before the open after reporting that its Phase 3 trial PIVOT-006 met its main goal: its drug cretostimogene cut the risk of the cancer returning by 68% (hazard ratio 0.32, 95% interval 0.23 to 0.45, p below 0.0001) in intermediate-risk and high-grade Ta bladder cancer, with no severe treatment-related side effects. The company puts this group at about 50,000 patients with no approved treatment of this kind and plans a second application to the FDA in the second quarter of 2027 (reported, its filing). UroGen fell 10.2% in the same hours with no filing and no story of its own.
themes.mechanism: UroGen sells in the same disease. Its drug Zusduri made $68.0 million last quarter, its next version UGN-103 is under FDA review for low-grade intermediate-risk bladder cancer, and it plans a 2027 trial of UGN-103 as an add-on treatment in newly diagnosed intermediate-risk patients (its Nov 4 results release). That is the use CG Oncology has now shown a Phase 3 result in. That UroGen fell because of CG Oncology's result is my inference: no page I could read says so. The two did not move together over the past year (neither is among the other's partners), so the link is the disease, not a habit of moving together.
themes.name: Bladder cancer: CG Oncology's trial result, and UroGen falling beside it
themes.watch: Whether UroGen's fall holds once the session opens (it rests on seven pre-market prints) and whether the company or an analyst answers the result. The full data on Dec 2 at the urologic oncology meeting. A share sale by CG Oncology after the jump would fit its habit; that says nothing about the price.
